record.title: Anthropic reports Claude-designed binders for four scorpion neurotoxins, without neutralization evidence
record.summary: Anthropic’s Oct 20 technical report describes an internal Claude Science campaign against five medically relevant scorpion neurotoxins. From an initial prompt and four follow-ups, the system generated 318,484 designs and selected 180; the team added 31 designs for laboratory testing. The authors report that 17 of 211 designs met their binding criteria across four toxins, including two Cn2 binders with single-digit nanomolar affinity or tighter in the reported assays. None of 151 designs targeting multiple toxins met the criteria against more than one. The report and sequence/binding dataset are public. These are author-reported binding results: no neutralization, animal efficacy, matched expert/pipeline baseline, or therapeutic outcome is established.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report that 17 of 211 tested designs met their stated binding criteria for one of four scorpion toxins; none met criteria against Ts1.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report single-digit-nanomolar-or-tighter affinity estimates for Cn2-B1 in assays at both CROs and competition with the LR antibody.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: None of the 151 designs made against two or more toxins met the authors' binding criteria against more than one toxin.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The study did not test any binder for cellular neutralization or in-vivo efficacy and did not establish an antivenom.

evidence_gaps.description: No candidate was tested for neutralization of channel activity in vitro or for protection in animals; binding/antibody competition does not establish function.
Reported binder classifications and affinities have not been independently reanalyzed from released raw data or reproduced by an independent laboratory.
No matched expert or fixed-pipeline baseline was experimentally run; the reported compute/time cannot quantify comparative advantage.
No multi-toxin design met binding criteria against more than one target; mechanism of failure is unresolved.

brief.importance_rationale: If the reported assay results are valid, agent-directed design plus external laboratory testing produced measurable binders against several medically relevant toxins associated with under-served regions, a notable scientific and drug-discovery result. Its therapeutic consequence remains unproven because neutralization, animal efficacy, safety, cost, and matched expert or pipeline comparisons were not measured.
limitations: Binding was measured against recombinant toxins of undocumented activity; no design was tested for cellular neutralization or in-vivo efficacy, and no antivenom was produced.

The study reports 17 binders across four toxins, but LqhIII was tested at one lab only; affinity estimates rely on limited concentration-series/replicate conditions and some surface/fit limitations are reported.
Two Cn2 designs have reported low-nanomolar affinity and competition with LR, but competition is not a functional neutralization assay; the complexes are predicted and no design structure was solved.
None of 151 multi-toxin designs met the criteria against more than one toxin; the result may reflect model capability, prompting, tools or biological feasibility.
No expert or fixed-pipeline experimental baseline was run, so the report does not quantify model contribution or comparative time/cost savings.
The campaign used about 10,000 H100 GPU-hours and two CROs, limiting accessibility; claimed efficiency gains from separate work rely on in-silico scores and do not validate this experiment.
Safety, immunogenicity, serum half-life, stability, manufacturing cost, distribution and patient outcomes were not measured.
brief.summary: Anthropic’s Oct 20 technical report describes an internal Claude Science campaign against five medically relevant scorpion neurotoxins. From an initial prompt and four follow-ups, the system generated 318,484 designs and selected 180; the team added 31 designs for laboratory testing. The authors report that 17 of 211 designs met their binding criteria across four toxins, including two Cn2 binders with single-digit nanomolar affinity or tighter in the reported assays. None of 151 designs targeting multiple toxins met the criteria against more than one. The report and sequence/binding dataset are public. These are author-reported binding results: no neutralization, animal efficacy, matched expert/pipeline baseline, or therapeutic outcome is established.

technical.claimed_result: The authors report that 17 of 211 designs met their stated binder criteria across four toxins: seven for Cn2, four for AaH II, four for AaH I and two for LqhIII. The LqhIII results were measured at one lab only. The tightest Cn2 design, Cn2-B1, had reported single-digit nanomolar or tighter affinity estimates at both labs and competed with the LR antibody in a competition assay. None of the 151 multi-toxin designs met criteria against more than one toxin.
technical.compute_or_cost: The reported campaign used on the order of 10,000 H100 GPU-hours and two CROs. The authors note in separate work that a simplified prompt on one GPU for 24 hours achieved comparable in-silico scores to earlier campaigns using about 100 times more GPU-hours; that is not an experimental replication or measured cost reduction for this scorpion campaign.
technical.demonstrated_result: The primary report and released dataset document the authors' Oct 20 report and the 211 tested sequences/data. The experimental binding outcomes are reported by Anthropic and its two CRO collaborators and were not independently reproduced in this review.
technical.implementation_status: Research demonstration with a public report and released set of 211 designs and binding data. No therapeutic candidate has been shown to neutralize venom or protect cells/animals, and no clinical or manufacturing path is established.
technical.mechanism: The initial prompt set target toxins, binding sites, design sets, candidate tools and rules for novelty/scoring/selection. Across four follow-ups, Claude selected structures and hotspots, chose among 12 design tools, generated and filtered designs, and selected candidates for external assays. The campaign attempted both single-toxin and multi-toxin binders; only single-toxin designs met the authors' multi-lab binding criteria.
technical.novelty: The report presents a model-directed design campaign with external binding assays against scorpion toxins, including targets the authors say lacked prior de-novo binder reports. It also tests the more ambitious multi-toxin objective, which failed under the stated criteria.
technical.regime: One Anthropic internal-research-model campaign in Claude Science, beginning from a prompt plus four follow-ups, using five recombinant sodium-channel toxins selected across four regions. The authors report 318,484 generated designs, 180 selected by Claude plus 31 added with its help, ~10,000 H100 GPU-hours and 64 hours elapsed before the initial 180-design list. Adaptyv Bio and Twist Bioscience performed binding assays under specified hit/affinity/response/off-target criteria.
technical.reproducibility: The technical report, 211 designs, predicted structures/scores and experimental binding data are publicly accessible. No independent reproduction of the campaign, assays, or hit classification was performed here. The CROs used complementary expression/assay setups, but both results are reported by Anthropic and collaborators.
technical.strongest_baseline: No expert-designed or fixed-pipeline experimental baseline was run in this campaign. The report therefore cannot separate Claude's contribution from the design tools or quantify time/cost savings against a conventional campaign.

brief.title: Anthropic reports Claude-designed binders for four scorpion neurotoxins, without neutralization evidence
brief.why_it_matters: The result is a notable step in AI-assisted molecular design because two contract research organizations tested a large model-generated design set against medically relevant toxins. It shows reported binding activity across several targets, while also exposing a sharp boundary: every qualifying design was toxin-specific, and the multi-toxin campaign did not meet its stated objective. The work is not an antivenom result and does not establish that Claude’s contribution outperforms existing design pipelines.
